note: Authored once per finding, by hand, then only ever appended to. This file is a READ input to scripts/derive_documentation_model.py (like evaluation-baseline.json), never written by it, so the disposition counts in figure field-trial-disposition are sourced rather than counted by hand. A RESOLVED_IN_1_3_0 row always carries a non-empty control: a row whose fix has no control that stops it recurring is REMAINS_A_LIMITATION instead, even where the document narrates the fix under a 'what 1.3.0 resolved' heading as an honestly-caveated repair.

findings.statement: All 33 MODULE.md front matters declared framework_release: 1.0.0 while every sibling MODULE_MANIFEST.yaml declared the current release, and nothing compared the two representations of the same fact.
findings.control: four FRAMEWORK_STRUCTURE check codes plus two verifier_mutation_check.py controls (narrative_release_pin_drifts_from_manifest_and_VERSION, manifest_release_pin_drifts_from_VERSION), both measured caught

findings.statement: 09_tests_evals/TEST_MANIFEST.json named an obsolete suite (ABS.TEST.SUITE.FRAMEWORK.RC2, a 32-module fixture surface) against a 33-module registry. Its content is now correct for 1.3.0 (ABS.TEST.SUITE.FRAMEWORK.1.3.1; the measured 33/33/33/33 fixture surface; the V2 contract validator; the cross-representation pin; verifier liveness), but nothing in runtime/, tools/, or 09_tests_evals/ reads the file to check it against the registry it summarizes, so it is a description that can drift again silently.
findings.evidence: 09_tests_evals/TEST_MANIFEST.json; grep -rn "TEST_MANIFEST" runtime/ tools/ 09_tests_evals/ returns no reader

findings.statement: The 35 tracked .dot sources were rendered to .svg by two different Graphviz builds (32 by 2.42.4, 3 by 2.43.0), and neither build was recorded anywhere, so the byte-level parity check in FRAMEWORK_REPRESENTATION passed only on the original build host.
findings.evidence: LIMITATIONS.md (Visual derivatives / Environment); all 35 tracked module blueprint/*.svg now carry "Generated by graphviz version 15.1.0 (20260618.0150)"
findings.control: runtime/verify.py FRAMEWORK_REPRESENTATION visual-parity check, now exercised against one recorded, unanimous renderer build named in LIMITATIONS.md

findings.statement: The parity check strips only Graphviz's version comment from a derivative, so it is sensitive to the renderer build, not merely to the renderer's presence. A different build that changes layout or numeric formatting reports VISUAL_DERIVATIVE_STALE for every derivative even when no source changed.

release_tree_integrity requires the release root's basename to equal ROOT_NAME and denylists .git among FORBIDDEN_PARTS. At 1.1.0 the release directory was named subject; through 1.2.0 the repository's .git lived inside the release payload, so no working tree could ever pass release_tree_integrity — only a sealed zip could.
findings.evidence: repository root RELEASE_STAMP.json working_tree_note, stamped_utc 2026-09-06: "The working tree carries .git, which release_tree_integrity denylists by design."
findings.control: 01_control_plane/manifests_releases/tools/release_integrity.py ROOT_NAME check and FORBIDDEN_PARTS denylist (FRAMEWORK_IDENTITY section), now satisfiable because .git was moved to the repository root outside the payload

findings.statement: RELEASE_ALLOWLIST.json still declared ABS.RELEASE.1.0.0-RC3 and held 879 records against a 1,079-file tree, under a policy named EXACT_RECORD_SET_FAIL_CLOSED that nothing enforced. Its generator looked up BASELINE_CHAIN[0], which was RC2 on the RC3 line and became RC1 after the 1.2.0 merge, so every baseline it was handed was refused and nothing ever regenerated it.
findings.evidence: 01_control_plane/manifests_releases/tools/generate_release_allowlist.py verify_immutable_baseline(); RELEASE_ALLOWLIST.json now release_id ABS.RELEASE.1.3.1, record_count 1079
findings.control: runtime/verify.py section_governance's six ALLOWLIST_* check codes plus the allowlist_record_removed_while_file_remains mutation control, measured caught

findings.statement: docs/ultimate-engine/REGENERATE.md documented a two-directory layout (a sibling engine/ beside a directory named subject/) that this repository's layout does not have, so none of its commands could be run as written.
findings.note: The procedure was rewritten to match this layout, but nothing mechanically checks that REGENERATE.md's fenced commands still match the tree the next time the layout changes; this is a repair, not a control-backed resolution.

findings.statement: 01_control_plane/manifests_releases/tools/generate_release_allowlist.py refuses any baseline directory not named absolute-canonical-framework-v1.0.0-rc.2, verified against its own detached checksum ledger. That immutable RC2 tree was not previously distributed with the repository, so a fresh clone could verify the committed allowlist but could not regenerate it.
findings.evidence: the sealed absolute-canonical-framework-v1.0.0-rc.2.zip and its detached .sha256 are committed under _release/predecessors/, alongside the full BASELINE_CHAIN (RC1, RC2, 1.0.0, 1.1.0, 1.2.0)
findings.control: a clone extracts the committed, checksum-verified RC2 archive into the gitignored predecessor/ directory and runs generate_release_allowlist.py against it; verify_immutable_baseline() checks the extracted tree's basename and checksum ledger before the generator will use it

findings.statement: Internal deterministic verification demonstrates consistency in a named environment. It cannot make the runtime an independent certifier of its own artifact.
findings.evidence: LIMITATIONS.md (Certification); runtime/verify.py section_governance NONWAIVABLE_CONTROL_WEAKENED on ABS.CFG.RELEASE.SELF_CERTIFICATION

findings.statement: The local hash chain detects edited, removed, or reordered entries. A writer with full control of the chain can recompute it from genesis; only a detached anchor stored outside that writer's sole control adds full-rewrite detection.
Every work packet records a rollback statement; the runtime checks it for presence, never for correctness or feasibility, and never executes or rehearses it.

Mutating commands are serialized with an advisory flock on .absolute/.lock for the whole operation, which is safe for one host and does not coordinate two hosts sharing a project over a network filesystem.

The framework deliberately keeps no exclusion list outside the control-plane process records, so ordinary version-control activity or a generated cache can invalidate evidence bound to the previous tree identity. 1.3.0 removed the largest instance of this cost (.git moving outside the payload); the property itself — no exclusion list — is unchanged.

The deep verifier proves internal completeness and consistency from raw bytes. It does not prove a document is correct about the world, and no provider host, remote, credential, production project, publication service, or external certifier is exercised by the package-local suite.
findings.evidence: LIMITATIONS.md (Scope of the deep verifier); 09_tests_evals/TEST_MANIFEST.json limitations

findings.statement: tools/verifier_mutation_check.py proves liveness only for the defect classes named in its own MUTATIONS list. It is not a proof that every check in the deep verifier is alive, and there are no unit tests for runtime/ beyond the two harnesses (deep_verify.py and verifier_mutation_check.py).
The vendored Ultimate Engine's own health check does not report a clean run on itself; this is the instrument's self-state, not a claim about the subject release.
findings.evidence: engine/CHANGELOG.md [1.0.5]; measured 2026-09-07 as 28 pass / 5 fail / 5 skip (CONS-11, BUILD-01, BUILD-03, SUITE-03, SUITE-05) at Ultimate Engine 1.0.5, distinct from the 2026-09-01 engine-on-subject baseline of 3 pass / 28 fail / 7 skip recorded in evaluation-baseline.json

findings.statement: The engine's document lifecycle describes a final content-certifying stamp but documents no single command that creates one; applying a stamp requires knowledge of the comment grammar in tools/docgen/identity.py and a two-commit procedure.
No documented engine command initializes a new host project's rule layer, system spec, or project index from nothing; each was hand-authored for this subject.

tools.health's engine-on-subject run assumes its --root is also the engine repository, so it asks a foreign host to contain the engine's own process documents, Git hook source, renderer packages, retained tests, and graph builders. Most of the 2026-09-01 baseline's failures measure this portability assumption, not missing subject documentation.

tools.blueprint derives its module map only from tracked Python files, so it cannot discover a canonical module whose authority lives entirely in Markdown, YAML, JSON, schemas, or fixtures. Its generated blueprint is an honest map of the executable layer, never a complete map of a representation-heavy framework like this one.
findings.evidence: blueprint/SYSTEM.md "The system, in containers"; docs/ultimate-engine/SYS-110-architecture.md "Representations are the architecture"

findings.statement: tools.corpus_check writes a host-local run log (<root>/.docgen/corpus_check/runs.jsonl) by default, which changes a subject whose own identity model includes every file under the payload root.

The engine's present-tense and cross-reference guards can treat a runtime-created .absolute/ path as an absent product claim in a pristine, not-yet-installed framework release, rather than recognizing it as correctly absent before installation.
findings.evidence: engine field-trial finding, carried unchanged from the 2026-09-01 documentation pass

findings.statement: Engine guidance disagrees with itself about numeric figure provenance: the document-engine skill states an unsourced value fails closed, while INTERPRETATION.md and the sidecar-loading code treat the data_sources convention as advisory.

A <!-- figure:ID --> directive with no matching sidecar entry is documented as silently omitted from the rendered document rather than refused at build time, which is a false-green shape (a missing figure looks like a clean build) with no red-first test in the engine's own audit for that specific behavior.
